method: IRONMAN's official 2026 performance-based qualification, implemented from public data. Each age-group winner earns an automatic World Championship slot; the remaining slots go to the athletes whose age-graded time (finish ÷ their age-group Kona Standard) ranks highest in a single global ranking across all age groups and both genders. The Kona Standard is the average of the fastest 20% of World Championship finish times over the last 5 editions (Kona and Nice), per age group per gender. Each race uses a fixed slot allocation (~40, larger for a few big races). Qualifying time = the slowest finish time that still earned a slot. Independent historical estimate — not a guarantee: roll-down softens the real cutoff. Figures are the median of the last editions with a min–max range.
